pages.scan: Top wide panel: caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' The doctor in a white coat stands in a doorway with her hand out, welcoming an elderly woman in a purple sari, while two patients wait on metal chairs at right. Bottom-left: a receptionist in a blue kurta holds a phone and writes in a ledger. Her upper-left balloon reads 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...' and the lower-right one reads 'I wish everything were easier to manage!' Bottom-right: the doctor, hand on chin, watches the receptionist in the background and says 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.'
pages.observation: All three tails clearly reach the right head: the receptionist's two balloons and the doctor's balloon. No balloon covers a face, the phone or the writing hand. The two receptionist balloons are stepped so the higher-left one reads first, which is natural. The doctor's line works as a quiet resolve to herself, since the receptionist is still on the phone, though it is a little unclear whether she is saying it to her. 'Belongs with patients' reads slightly awkwardly. The receptionist is never named.

pages.scan: Top panel at sunset: caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' and teal label 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic'. The doctor types on a laptop showing an onboarding form. Middle-left: the doctor, finger to chin at the laptop, says 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' Middle-right: the receptionist, small in a separate office, holds up a phone and says 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' Teal label 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff' sits there too. Bottom panel: the seated doctor raises a fist and says 'One team. Better coordination.' The receptionist stands beside her smiling silently and holds a phone with a calendar app.
pages.observation: All tails reach the intended speaker: doctor, receptionist, doctor. The 'And our team...' line follows on from the doctor's line, but the receptionist is in a different room in that panel. Readers may wonder whether these two are talking to each other or delivering separate pitch lines. The top caption overlaps the doctor's hair bun but not her face. The 'WELBUK CARE' label covers the receptionist's lower legs and feet, which matters little, and her phone stays visible. The bottom balloon sits between the two faces and covers neither. The sunset windows in the first three panels disappear in the bottom panel, a small time-continuity gap.

pages.scan: Panel 1: a man in a green shirt with a shoulder bag waves as he enters through a glass door and says 'Good morning! I'd like to see the doctor.' The receptionist at her computer in the foreground looks up. Panel 2: the receptionist gestures and says 'Of course. May I register your details for today's appointment?' The man's back and the hand holding his phone are in the foreground. Panel 3: the man, eyes closed and smiling, says 'Yes, please.' while she types. Panel 4: she gestures toward the seats and says 'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' He stands holding his bag strap.
pages.observation: Tails in panels 1 to 3 reach the right person. Panel 1's long horizontal tail ends at his raised hand by his face rather than at his mouth, but it is still unambiguous. Panel 4's balloon has no visible tail, and its bottom edge cuts across the top of the receptionist's hair and head. Her eyes stay visible and the speaker is only implied by proximity, so please check that. 'Ravi' is used without the reader seeing him give his name, which the registration implies but never shows. 'Good morning' follows the sunset onboarding on page 2 with no time-skip cue. The phone sits on the desk in panel 1, is in the man's hand in panel 2 and is on the desk in front of him in panel 3, a minor continuity question.

pages.scan: Panel 1, consulting room: the doctor gestures across the desk with a closed laptop and says 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' Ravi sits relaxed. Panel 2: Ravi rubs his neck and says 'I've been feeling tired lately.' The doctor's back is in the foreground. Panel 3, no dialogue: caption 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' The doctor listens with hands clasped, Ravi's back in the foreground. Panel 4: the doctor gestures and says 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' Ravi nods.
pages.observation: Tails reach the doctor in panels 1 and 4 and Ravi in panel 2, and no balloon covers a face or hand. The panel 3 caption box cuts into the top of the doctor's head down to just above her eyes. Her expression still reads, but the crop is tight. The caption comes between the symptom and the reply, and the reply is generic. It never answers 'tired' directly, so the exchange feels a little like narration over a conversation. It does not skip an answer, but it is light on the doctor's actual reaction.

pages.scan: Panel 1, back at reception: the receptionist points at Ravi's phone and says 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' Panel 2: Ravi holds up the phone with a calendar and heart app and says 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' Teal label 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients' at bottom-left. Panel 3: the receptionist gestures and says 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' Ravi's shoulder and phone are in the foreground. Panel 4: caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' Ravi walks out waving while the doctor and receptionist wave from the glass door.
pages.observation: Tails in panels 1 and 2 clearly reach the receptionist and Ravi. Panel 3's tail is almost invisible, a tiny stub at the balloon's bottom edge just above her head, so the speaker comes only from proximity. The panel 2 label comes very close to Ravi's left fingers on the phone but leaves the phone screen clear. The move from the consulting room on page 4 back to the reception desk has no transition cue. The offered walkthrough is not shown before he leaves, which is acceptable as an ellipsis. The question and answer read in the right order with no skipped reply.

pages.scan: Panel 1: Ravi sits on a train with a phone, looking out at a city. Caption: 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' Panel 2, soft vignette edges: teal 'WELBUK VISION' label and caption 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' An older grey-haired doctor in glasses stands before another building. Panel 3: a second 'WELBUK VISION' label and caption 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' Ravi, a woman in yellow holding a tablet and a boy look at it on a sofa. Panel 4: the receptionist, doctor and Ravi, who is waving, stand in front of the clinic. Label 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health' and caption 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.'
pages.observation: There are no speech balloons or tails on this page, only captions and labels. 'Tomorrow' could mean the next day or the future in general. Why Ravi is on a train is unexplained. The older doctor, the woman and the child are not introduced, so the reader has to guess at a specialist and Ravi's family. The vignette helps signal that this is imagined. The same 'WELBUK VISION' label in two neighbouring panels is redundant. The panel 4 caption covers the receptionist's and doctor's lower legs, which matters little. No caption covers a face, the tablet or the phone. The ending reads as a promotional group shot more than a story beat.
